question: Were you married at the end of last year, and does anyone live with you that you support?
why_ask: Filing status sets the standard deduction, tax rates and filing threshold.
retrieval_query: how to choose filing status single head of household

question: Were you (or your spouse, if filing jointly) born before January 2, 1961?
why_ask: Taxpayers 65 or older get a larger standard deduction federally and a senior exemption credit in California.
retrieval_query: standard deduction age 65 or older additional amount

question: Did you live in California for all of last year?
why_ask: Full-year residents file Form 540; part-year residents and nonresidents file Form 540NR.

question: Did you work or earn any income in a state other than California last year?
why_ask: Income earned in another state can create a filing requirement there.
retrieval_query: California other state tax credit nonresident income

question: What is the total in Box 1 of all your W-2 forms?
why_ask: Wages are the main income line; withholding on the W-2 is credited against the tax.

question: Did you have more than one employer during the year?
why_ask: With two or more employers, too much Social Security tax may have been withheld and can be claimed back.
retrieval_query: excess social security tax withheld more than one employer

question: Is there anyone, such as a child or a relative, whom you supported and who lived with you?
why_ask: Dependents can change filing status and qualify for several credits.
retrieval_query: who qualifies as a dependent qualifying child qualifying relative

question: Is any of those children under 17 at the end of the year?
why_ask: A qualifying child under 17 may qualify for the Child Tax Credit.
retrieval_query: child tax credit qualifying child under age 17

question: Is any child under 6 at the end of the year?
why_ask: California's Young Child Tax Credit applies to a child under 6 when the family qualifies for CalEITC.

question: Did you pay for daycare or babysitting so that you could work?
why_ask: Work-related care costs may qualify for the Child and Dependent Care Credit.
required_docs: childcare provider name, address and tax ID
retrieval_query: child and dependent care credit work-related expenses

question: Did you pay interest on a student loan last year?
why_ask: Student loan interest may be deductible even without itemizing.

question: How much student loan interest did you pay (Form 1098-E, Box 1)?
why_ask: The deduction is limited and phases out at higher incomes.

question: Did you or your employer put money into a Health Savings Account (HSA)?
why_ask: HSA contributions are deductible federally, but California does not follow this, so they are added back on Schedule CA.
retrieval_query: health savings account California adjustment Schedule CA
source: IRS Pub 969; FTB Schedule CA (540) instructions

question: Did you rent the home you lived in, in California, for at least half the year?
why_ask: California renters below an income limit may claim the nonrefundable renter's credit.
